title: HITL annotation adapter wire protocol (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working sketch for a lightweight human-in-the-loop (HITL) annotation adapter service and the wire protocol needed to integrate Redwood runtime evaluation hooks with human labelers and micro-labeling UIs. Goal: minimal surface area, observable, resumable, and easy to plugin behind the existing runtime routing system.

Context / motivation:
- We need a simple bridge for streaming candidate responses (or partial responses) out to labelers, capture token-level or response-level annotations, and feed them back into the system via small payloads (labels, comment, confidence, edits).
- Primary consumer: evaluation pipelines, QA playbooks, and small-scale live labeling for model quality regressions.
- Constraints: low operational overhead, audit trail, retry/resume semantics, secure ephemeral credentials, and bounded cost when traffic spikes.

Actors:
- Inference Runtime (producer): emits annotation tasks when a request matches sampling rules (per-route eval set, regression alarm, manual "send to HITL").
- Adapter Service (this spec): accepts tasks, shards to available labelers / UIs, manages state, records events/edits, and returns final artifact (label bundle).
- Labeler UI (consumer): web or mobile interface used by human annotators, connected via websocket or polled REST endpoints.
- Feedback Sink: internal service that consumes finalized labels for training/metrics (can be S3 topic or evaluation job).

Design goals / non-goals:
- Support streaming and non-streaming modes.
- Task-level idempotency and resume: labeler can disconnect and resume, partial annotations preserved.
- Compact payloads: avoid shipping full dialogs if not needed (use references to stored artifacts).
- Telemetry-friendly: every state transition emits a tenant-scoped event for cost/latency accounting.
- Security: short-lived tokens, tenant isolation, and redaction options for PII.
- Non-goal: high-throughput annotation platform for thousands of labelers (we expect small, curated teams initially).

High-level wire shapes:
1) Task envelope (from runtime -> adapter):
- POST /v1/tasks
  {
    "task_id": "t_01GX4...",
    "tenant_id": "acme-inc",
    "route": "/chat/generate",
    "model": "gptx-13b-quant",
    "trigger_reason": "sampling:regression_watchlist",
    "payload_ref": "s3://internal/eval/prefix/resp-2024-11-12-1234.json",
    "inline_payload": null, // optional small text blob if not using ref
    "requirements": {"min_labels": 3, "label_types": ["quality","toxicity"], "expires_at": "2024-12-10T12:00:00Z"},
    "priority": "low|normal|high",
    "metadata": {"ingest_route": "canary-11", "sample_seed": "8943"}
  }
Notes: payload_ref is preferred for large context. Adapter must fetch ref with runtime role; runtime may supply presigned url in metadata.

2) Subscription / assignment (adapter -> labeler UI):
- Websocket channel per labeler / per-queue: ws://adapter/v1/subscribe?queue=acme-inc-quality&token=ephemeral
- Message types: TASK_ASSIGN, TASK_UPDATE, HEARTBEAT, ACK.
- TASK_ASSIGN payload includes task_id, minimal payload (title, snippet, link to full context), labeling schema, time budget.

Task lifecycle states (adapter internal): queued -> assigned -> in_progress -> submitted -> verified -> archived | cancelled
Each transition emits telemetry: {task_id, state, ts, actor, annotation_count, duration_ms}.

3) Annotation submission (labeler -> adapter):
- POST /v1/tasks/{task_id}/annotations
  {
    "labeler_id": "u_3292",
    "annotation_id": "a_1290",
    "type": "quality", // or multi-type payloads
    "value": "3", // numeric/choice/string depending on schema
    "span": {"start": 34, "end": 88}, // optional token/char span referencing inline payload or stored ref
    "comment": "model hallucinated a date",
    "confidence": 0.7,
    "partial": false, // partial = true to save draft
    "edits": [ {"op":"replace","start":0,"end":120,"text": "Corrected answer: ..."} ],
    "client_ts": "2024-12-05T16:22:11Z"
  }
- Response: 202 Accepted with location header /v1/tasks/{task_id}/annotations/{annotation_id}

4) Finalization / review flow:
- When requirements.min_labels satisfied and annotations verified (optional verification worker), the adapter posts to feedback sink:
  POST /v1/feedback 
  { "task_id": "t_...", "tenant_id": "acme-inc", "final_labels_ref": "s3://.../t_.../bundle.json", "metrics": {"label_agreement": 0.78}, "annotations_count": 3 }
- Feedback sink should support batching and idempotent ingestion (accept same bundle multiple times safely).

Backpressure and cost control:
- Sampling rules in runtime should limit tasks per-minute per-tenant. Adapter enforces queue depth caps (configurable per-tenant).
- If adapter queue is full, runtime receives 429 with a hint header X-Adapter-Backpressure-Until: <ts>. Runtime can drop or delay the sample.
- For ephemeral spikes, adapter supports a "deferred-accept" mode where tasks are stored with low priority and only surfaced during work hours.

Security / credentials:
- Labeler UIs authenticate via short-lived JWTs minted by adapter auth service. JWT contains: labeler_id, scopes (read:queue_name, write:task_id), exp.
- Adapter-to-runtime fetches payload_ref via short-lived presigned link or uses internal service account. All activity logs must include actor.
- PII redaction: tasks can include redaction hints (metadata.redact: ["email","ssn"]) and tool may run automated redaction before sending to labelers.

Telemetry and observability:
- Minimal event set: task.created, task.assigned, task.started, annotation.created, annotation.partial_saved, task.submitted, task.closed, task.failed.
- Tag events with tenant_id, route, model, sampling_reason, and cost_bucket (manual). Keep payloads out of main telemetry stream (use refs).
- Metric ideas: mean time to annotation, labeler churn, annotation agreement, cost per labeled task.

Edge cases / failure modes:
- Labeler disconnects mid-annotate: save draft (partial=true) and allow resume.
- Duplicate annotations: deduplicate by annotation_id + labeler_id; accept last-writer within a window if partial drafts.
- Missing payload_ref: adapter should reject task with 422 and include a retryable flag; runtime should resend with inline_payload or presigned url.
- Overlapping edits: edits array must be applied in order; adapter can provide simple three-way merge for text edits (best-effort) and attach conflicts to verification queue.

API contract examples (compact):
- Create task: POST /v1/tasks -> 201 {"task_id": "t_...", "assigned_queue": "acme-inc-quality"}
- Poll annotations: GET /v1/tasks/{task_id}/annotations -> [ {annotation objects} ]
- Stream assign: TASK_ASSIGN -> {task_id, snippet, schema, due_seconds}

Local dev mode and testing:
- Provide an "echo" mode where runtime can POST with inline_payload and adapter immediately returns a testable bundle with fake labelers (useful for integration tests).
- Docker compose with in-memory store (redis for queues, sqlite for metadata) and a mock feedback sink.

Acceptance criteria for MVP:
- End-to-end flow: runtime -> adapter -> mock labeler -> adapter -> feedback sink with idempotent ingestion and task audit log.
- Support for partial saves and resume.
- Basic telemetry and tenant-level queue caps.
- Security: short-lived labeler tokens and presigned payload fetching.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Label schema language: simple JSON schema vs shipped proto? (lean: JSON schema v4).
- Verification step: who runs verification (adapter-run worker vs separate service)?
- Richer editing primitives: are ops sufficient or do we need OT/CRDT for heavy edit workflows?
- UI needs checklist: batch labeling, keyboard shortcuts, disagreement triage view. Ask UX.

Next steps (short):
- Spike a minimal adapter service (2-week) with in-memory queue, a simple labeler web UI, and a fake feedback sink.
- Run integration test with runtime sampler (use existing sampling sandbox).
- Prototype telemetry pipeline and dashboards (per-tenant).

Notes to self / scribbles:
- Consider exposing a small onboarding API for external vendors (e.g., Scale, Labelbox) to poll tasks without websockets. That should be an opt-in integration with RBAC.
- Keep audit trail: every annotation mutation should be append-only in main store; tombstone if deleted.
- Might be useful to reuse existing session-authn tokens for labeler auth in enterprise customers (mapping tenant labeler groups).

Snippets / example JSON schema (very rough):
- label_schema: {"fields": [{"id":"quality","type":"rating","scale":[1,5],"required":true},{"id":"toxicity","type":"multiselect","options":["none","mild","severe"]}]}

Sketch of minimal sequence diagram (text):
runtime -> adapter: POST /v1/tasks
adapter -> queue: push(task)
labeler UI -> adapter: ws subscribe
queue -> adapter: assign(task)
adapter -> labeler UI: TASK_ASSIGN
labeler UI -> adapter: POST /v1/tasks/{id}/annotations (possibly partial)
adapter -> feedback-sink: POST /v1/feedback (when done)

References:
- internal: /confluence/eval/hitl-playbook (TODO link)
- github: github.com/redwood-inference/hitl-adapter (prototype branch)

End of draft.

(If I come back later: sketch sample telemetry event format, add migration plan from current manual labeling folders, and draft sample UI wireframe text.)
